# Vertical margin anchors

Original OOXML controls generated by tools/vertical_margin_anchor_fixture.py,
using the repository-authored table-global-anchors package as boilerplate.
No corpus artwork or third-party engine is included. Each compatibility mode
(15 and 12) has 18 pages: topMargin/bottomMargin crossed with body/cell/
layoutInCell=false cell placement and numeric offset/center/bottom alignment.
The page is 720pt high with top/bottom margins of 54/90pt. Pictures are 72x36pt.

The reference application exported the PDFs. The recorder captures PDF image
bounds, hashes and page PNGs. All 36 native pages were visually inspected.
Body image Y positions are 12/9/18pt for topMargin and 642/657/684pt for
bottomMargin. Cell pictures use Y=86pt for the 12pt offset and Y=74pt for
both alignments, irrespective of which margin is named. In mode 15 this also
holds when layoutInCell=false. Mode 12 honors false and uses the body positions.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.4.2.3, 20.4.2.11 and 20.4.3.5 specify the anchor,
vertical position and reference bases. Body positions use the literal margin
bands. The reference application's cell-origin substitution, ignored vertical alignment and modern
handling of layoutInCell=false are compatibility behavior, rather than literal
page-margin coordinates. The source attributes remain intact on export.

Unit checks cover native frames, hit testing, no-edit package identity, text
editing, export/reopen and exact undo. Browser checks compare blue image masks
in both directions within one pixel on every page before/after editing and
reopening. These masks establish drawing placement, not complete glyph fidelity.
